text.p: A moderate earthquake shook the island of Hawaii early on Monday, the U.S. Geological Survey reported.

The quake had a preliminary magnitude of 5.3, rated as moderate on the open-ended Richter scale. The temblor was widely felt through the island, but there were no immediate reports of damage or injuries, according to the survey's Rebecca Phipps.
The quake, which occurred at 5:48 a.m. local time (1548 GMT) was centred near the southeast coast of the island, about 25 miles (40.2 km) south of the city of Hilo, Phipps said.
This was the largest earthquake on the island since a quake measuring 5.6 on February 1, 1994, she said.
